stem:
Anvi studies the diagram of two rectangles. Both have perimeter $24\,\mathrm{cm}$. Rectangle $P$ is $8\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $4\,\mathrm{cm}$; rectangle $Q$ is $9\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $3\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Which claim correctly decides what the equal perimeters tell about area?

options.text: The areas must be equal because both shapes are labelled with the word perimeter.
The perimeters match but the areas differ ($32\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ versus $27\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$), so perimeter alone does not fix area.
Each area is $24\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ because $24$ is the number printed as the perimeter.

teacher.key_rationale: P has area 32 and Q has area 27 while both perimeters are 24, so equal perimeter does not force equal area. Naming perimeter, assuming equal areas, or copying 24 as area miss that.
teacher.figure_note: Added two labelled rectangles P (8 by 4) and Q (9 by 3) with side lengths marked.
